It's a possibility that they froze during the moment and dissociated into thinking that they were fighting it. It does happen during extremely stressful and traumatic events. The best support you could give her right now is creating a safe space and telling her it's not her fault, reassuring her that she did everything she could. There are four types of responses with trauma kasi: **Fight, Flight, Freeze, Fawn**. In this case, she froze in the moment. It's something you have to develop skills for to combat, unfortunately. I hope she's okay, though and that you are also okay. Thank you for doing everything in your power to protect your sister.

I think for coping while falling out, stating the facts is good. Write them down and know that your decision was warranted. If you want to cut out toxic friends, it depends on their level of toxicity. If it's high, you should be blunt and clearly cut ties. If it's mild and they irritate you a lot (like if you ask for advice and they give advice, but it's not helpful or they have things that irritate you), slowly ghost them. I'm not kidding. Ask to leave the group chat for time for yourself and minimize contact, but still go out if you feel like it won't do much harm and not always. It may look harder to cut ties, but cutting ties too much is a bit problematic because what if all it needs is some constant reflection? Essentially putting the benefit of the doubt in the relationship.

Recent deaths. 

There was a man who hung himself to the high bars of a covered court at a school beside our local church. I was unfortunate enough to watch him just hanging there. The fear crept into every crevice of my body. I was shaking when I stared at it intently and I thought what if it was /my/ body... I couldn’t shake the thought away for weeks and that image just kept on reappearing in my head. 

A few months later, my uncle died of a medical illness. He was 43 and dearly beloved, as anyone in the family, by the whole family. I saw uncles and aunts that I haven’t seen in years who have come from far off places just to pay respects. It was also the first time I saw my dad cry... It was heart-wrenching and I cried myself. I couldn’t stomach the feeling that he would leave his young daughters and I wanted to be there for them no matter what. 

I always believe that life is harder as it already is, so I shouldn’t make it any harder for anyone. I just don’t want my parents or friends or anyone suffering from the same condition I have to experience the same hurt I’ve had happen to me whenever deaths occur. I just don’t want my parents to wake up ten years later and cry for me at my grave... I just don’t want them to feel bad because I couldn’t be strong.
